question: A classification subagent must always emit a structured label using one of its provided tools (e.g. tag_urgent, tag_normal, tag_spam) and must never return free-text commentary instead of a call, though which specific tag applies depends on the message content. Which tool_choice setting guarantees this behavior?
options: A) tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "tag_normal"}, which forces the same tag every time regardless of message content
B) tool_choice: {"type": "any"}, which requires the model to call one of the provided tools without pinning it to a specific one
C) tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}, which lets the model decide whether calling a tag tool or replying in prose better fits the message
D) tool_choice: {"type": "none"}, which stops the model from calling any tag tool and relies on prompt wording instead
correct_answers: B) tool_choice: {"type": "any"}, which requires the model to call one of the provided tools without pinning it to a specific one
explanations: Incorrect. Forcing a single named tool would apply the same tag on every message regardless of content, which contradicts the need for the correct tag to vary by message.

Correct. "any" tells the model it must use one of the provided tools without forcing a particular one, guaranteeing a structured tool call while still letting the model pick the tag that matches the message.

Incorrect. "auto" leaves the choice of calling a tool at all up to the model, which does not guarantee a structured tag is always produced, undermining the requirement for consistent structured output.
Incorrect. "none" blocks tool calls entirely, so the model could only respond in prose, which is the opposite of the required structured-output guarantee.
